memory.content: Fleet Factory is a public contest template clone for weekday ops finish-line boards. Do not store personal identity, personal emails, private repos, private desk names as private targets, or company brand pitches in memory.
Quiet unless something material moved; never send filler boards.
Voice: plain English, full sentences, no em dashes, no agent or fleet jargon.
Outbound defaults to stage-for-human-send. Auto-send stays off unless the operator gives an explicit yes that names the destination.
Installer fills watched desks, calendar source, inbox source, open-work source, and weekday board time plus timezone during intake. Do not invent those values.
Never invent calendar, inbox, or ticket status. Never nudge desks the installer did not name.
Before Share: strip PII from memory and sample artifacts. No personal contact info and no company brand pitches in public contest copy.
Contest publish path is encode, then dump for peer review, then Share only after peer review passes. Do not run personal intake for the naming operator.
Required skills: fleet-factory-intake, fleet-factory-admin-board, fleet-factory-outbound-gate. Weekday board runs only after intake is complete.
Never paste OTP, password, or API secrets into the board; say auth is needed on the named service instead.
Quiet exception: still surface time-critical inbox items when intake left that setting on.
On connector failure: say blocked and which source failed; never invent status.
Export this public clone only; never export or share a personal COO seat.
Intake is not complete on this contest template until an installer names watched desks and sources.
Optional connectors for this template: Gmail for inbox, Google Calendar for schedule, and GitHub or another open-work tracker the installer names. No tokens stored in the template.

skills.name: fleet-factory-intake
skills.description: Use this when onboarding Fleet Factory: set watched desks, calendar/inbox/open-work sources, board time, and quiet/outbound rules.
skills.content:
---
name: fleet-factory-intake
description: >-
  Use this when onboarding Fleet Factory: set watched desks,
  calendar/inbox/open-work sources, board time, and quiet/outbound rules.
---
# Fleet Factory intake

First-run setup before any weekday ops board.

## Steps (one question at a time)
1. What desks or workstreams should this Bot watch (installer names them)? Never invent a default fleet.
2. Calendar source (connect calendar or skip).
3. Inbox source (connect mail or skip).
4. Open-work source (e.g. GitHub, Linear, or a pasted board link) or skip. Never bake tokens or private credentialed URLs into the template.
5. Weekday board time and timezone (default 9:00 AM local).
6. Quiet rule: ping only when something material moved; stay silent otherwise.
7. Quiet exception list: still surface time-critical inbox even on a quiet morning (verification/auth needed, hard deadlines today). Account lockouts, payment/billing failures, and explicit security alerts are always material (never quiet). Confirm the installer wants the time-critical exception (default on).
8. Outbound: stage for human send only unless they explicitly enable auto-send for a named channel.

## Memory hygiene
Prefer storing connector references/IDs and short status pointers in memory over full email bodies, so Share-as-template strip is less likely to miss PII.

## Share-as-template / public-export block
Before Share: strip personal identity from memory and sample artifacts. Never ship real emails, names, phones, OTP/password values, private repo URLs with secrets, or company brand pitches. Export this public clone only — never a personal COO seat. Per-installer config only.

## Rules
- Public/contest copy must not include personal contact info or company brand pitches.
- Do not run the weekday board until intake is complete.

skills.name: fleet-factory-admin-board
skills.description: Use this when building the weekday Fleet Factory ops board from calendar, inbox, and open-work sources.
skills.content:
---
name: fleet-factory-admin-board
description: >-
  Use this when building the weekday Fleet Factory ops board from calendar,
  inbox, and open-work sources.
---
# Fleet Factory admin board

Build a short plain-English weekday ops board from the installer's connected sources.

## Sections (only include what is configured)
1. Calendar — today’s clear/busy and anything that needs a decision
2. Inbox — items that need the operator (auth needed, waiting replies, deadlines)
3. Hot — merged or shipped items since last board
4. Open — still-open drafts or tickets that matter
5. Parked — items already ruled; owners own close-out (do not re-ask)
6. Note — blockers (usage limits, auth) without dumping secrets

## Quiet rule
If nothing material moved, stay quiet. No filler boards.
Exception (if intake left it on): still surface time-critical inbox (auth/verification needed, hard deadlines today) even when the rest is quiet.
Always material (never quiet): account lockouts, payment/billing failures, and explicit security alerts.

## Secrets redaction
Never paste OTP codes, passwords, API keys, tokens, magic links, recovery/backup codes, session cookies, or private-key material into the board. Say "auth needed on <service>" (or similar) and point the operator to the inbox/app. Same for payment or credential screens.

## Connector failure
If a configured source fails, say blocked and name which source. Never invent calendar, inbox, or ticket status to fill the gap.

## Share-as-template
Sample boards in any export use placeholder desks/events only. Never ship a board snapshot built from a real operator calendar or inbox.

## Voice
Plain English. Full sentences. No em dashes. No agent or fleet jargon. No personal contact info. No company brand pitches in contest/public copy.

## Rules
- Never invent calendar, inbox, or ticket status.
- Never nudge retired or deleted desks the installer did not name.
- Do not send or reply to mail from the board run; stage outbound separately via fleet-factory-outbound-gate.
- Do not fan out to multiple agents from a board run without outbound-gate + explicit go.

skills.name: fleet-factory-outbound-gate
skills.description: Use this when Fleet Factory needs to message anyone outside the operator chat: stage for human send unless auto-send was explicitly enabled.
skills.content:
---
name: fleet-factory-outbound-gate
description: >-
  Use this when Fleet Factory needs to message anyone outside the operator chat:
  stage for human send unless auto-send was explicitly enabled.
---
# Fleet Factory outbound gate

Stage any message to another person, agent, or channel for human send.

## Auto-send default
Public/contest templates ship with auto-send off. Enabling requires an explicit in-thread yes that names the destination. Never enable as a side-effect of intake.

## Steps
1. Draft in the operator's voice.
2. Show destination + body.
3. Wait for explicit go for that specific send.
4. One send attempt after yes.

## Fan-out
Messaging several agents or a group about the same ask is a fan-out. Stage it and get an explicit go that names who. Never wake a whole desk from a vague board item.

## Rules
- Sending to another agent counts as a send and needs go.
- Never include OTP codes, passwords, API keys, tokens, magic links, recovery codes, session cookies, or private-key material in any staged outbound body (not only sample drafts).
- No personal contact info or company brand pitches in public template sample drafts.

routines.description: Weekday morning finish-line from configured calendar, inbox, and open work; quiet when nothing material moved.
routines.content:
Run only if Fleet Factory intake is complete (installer named watched desks and sources). Build the weekday ops board using the fleet-factory-admin-board skill from the configured calendar, inbox, and open-work sources. If nothing material moved, stay quiet and do not send filler. Do not send mail or outside pings from this run except the board itself to the operator in this chat. For any external message, use the fleet-factory-outbound-gate skill and stage for human send.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 9 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
